beats.narration_text: Here is the problem. A messy idea goes into Claude and a vague output comes out. What you need is a pipeline — nine skills from how-to-ai.guide that take your raw thought all the way to a ready-to-use prompt with a clear goal, full context, and your own voice.

card.sub: Nine slash-command skills form a pipeline from raw idea to a prompt with clear goal, full context, your voice.

beats.narration_text: The flow starts with your messy idea. Skill one: /prompt-master. Brain dump in, clean task spec out. Skill two: /grill-me — it asks questions until nothing is vague. Skill three: /how-to — it maps the steps you don't know yet. Skill four: /48 — the Optimizer, polishes your prompt specifically for Opus 4.8.

beats.narration_text: The flow continues. Skill five: /fable — same polish as the Optimizer but tuned for Fable 5. Skill six: /personal-voice — it tunes the draft to sound like you. Skill seven: /anti-ai — strips the AI tells from the output so it reads like a human wrote it.

beats.narration_text: The last two skills close the loop. Skill eight: /write-a-skill — it bottles your finished prompt as a reusable skill. Skill nine: /handoff — it creates a handoff document so the next Claude chat can pick up exactly where this one stopped. And that takes you from messy idea to a ready-to-use prompt: clear goal, full context, your voice.

beats.narration_text: You do not need all nine every time. For most tasks, start with /prompt-master. If the output still feels vague, run /grill-me. If you want it to sound like you, add /personal-voice. The skills travel with your Claude account — they are always one slash away.

card.sub: Start with /prompt-master. Add /grill-me if still vague. Add /personal-voice to sound like you. Find them free at how-to-ai.guide.

beats.narration_text: Here is what happens in practice. Before these skills: 'Write me a LinkedIn post about AI.' Claude guesses. It is fine. After running /prompt-master then /personal-voice: you get a full task spec with your tone, your audience, your goal — and the output sounds like a human actually wrote it.

Right side — AFTER label: two slash command badges '/prompt-master → /personal-voice' → polished output sample with visible structure lines (goal, tone, audience, draft).

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you want to get systematically better at prompting and you need a framework — not tips, a set of skills you can practice. Ask Claude to describe the nine prompt-writing skills, tell you which skill gap produces the most common failure mode in your workflow, and give you one deliberate practice exercise for the skill that's hardest to improve through trial and error alone.
